pages.title: Brightwell Supply Co.
pages.summary: Brightwell Supply Co. is a B2B industrial-supplies distributor selling fasteners, adhesives, sealants, and freight-heavy MRO consumables, operating out of a single warehouse in Stockton (Stockton warehouse).
pages.content:
Brightwell Supply Co. is a B2B industrial-supplies distributor selling fasteners, adhesives, sealants, and freight-heavy MRO consumables, operating out of a single warehouse in Stockton ([[stockton-warehouse]]). The business runs on tight peak-season logistics, a small number of large accounts, and a handful of key suppliers, with the fortnight covering a warehouse system cutover, a supplier renegotiation, and a customer escalation that reshaped a standing rule.

## What the team is working on

**CL Rollout: NexBin cutover** — Brightwell is mid-cutover from the legacy StockPro system ([[stockpro]]) to NexBin ([[nexbin]]), tracked as the CL Rollout project ([[cl-rollout]]). The Cutover Checklist has moved through revisions: v3.2's steps 7-8 require a full parallel cycle count (customer-owned) feeding into reconciling parallel count variance to zero (partner-owned) before cutover, and as of Nov 6, 2026 this pairing was not yet reflected in Brightwell's own cutover runbook [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-parallel-cycle-count-gap]. Brightwell is also still waiting on NexBin to confirm two vendor-owned steps — scheduling vendor case queue coverage for cutover day and confirming the rollback environment snapshot was taken (steps 12-13) — which Brightwell cannot self-certify [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-vendor-confirmation-pending-steps-12-13]. Checklist v3.3, mirrored Nov 12, 2026, adds a new customer-owned step 11: freeze inbound receipts at 12:00 the day before cutover to lock counted stock levels and reduce reconciliation variance at go-live, wording that matches what Purchasing had already logged independently [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-v33-freeze-inbound-receipts-step].

**Vantek Adhesives relationship** — Following a field action, Vantek Adhesives ([[vantek-adhesives]]) is shipping GripLoc 275 ([[griploc-275]]) orders on one-way pallets due to a returnable-pallet shortage, with Brightwell's dock breaking down and scrapping the pallets rather than returning them; this was confirmed via the PO-2026-1174 ASN received Nov 6, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-griploc275-one-way-pallets]. The previously discussed 4% Vantek volume rebate was never actually agreed — Dana Nwosu did not sign off — and is now treated as not agreed until further notice: not to be quoted, mentioned to customers, or built into margin projections, per Jonas Solheim's [[jonas]] Nov 10, 2026 account brief correction, which supersedes the earlier "pending paperwork" status [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-rebate-not-agreed-correction]. Separately, GripLoc 275 lead time from Vantek is confirmed at 5 business days from PO to dock, standard with no expedite needed, per Dana Nwosu's Nov 11, 2026 email to Jonas — this is the rep's figure by email rather than the 2027 price schedule, and Jonas is quoting it to Duraline Industrial Supply's Renee Alvarez for the GripLoc 275 add-on unless told otherwise [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-vantek-lead-time]. On the [[receiving]] side, a one-page "GripLoc 275 restock — receiving plan" (v1) was created Nov 12, 2026 for the dock, built from Vantek's order acknowledgment against the Nov 11 PO, covering ship date, freight mode, arrival window, pallet count, lot range, and a five-line checklist, with door assignment left to dispatch on the day [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-receiving-plan-doc-created]. For PO 78120 (GripLoc 275 restock, SO-114872), Vantek invoices at shipment as a single invoice dated the ship date, Nov 16, 2026, sent to Brightwell AP under current account-brief payment terms [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-78120-vantek-invoicing].

**Duraline Industrial Supply escalation** — Duraline ([[duraline]], [[duraline-industrial-supply]]) is a top-3 account for Brightwell [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-top3-account]. After a third late-cutoff incident that quarter, Brightwell granted a one-time waiver of its $150 expedite fee on PO 77812 on Nov 4, 2026, explicitly overriding the fee-scoring model; there is no standing policy waiving the fee, and a fourth incident would require an actual policy rather than another one-off exception [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-expedite-fee-no-standing-waiver]. Brightwell's same-day order cutoff during peak season is set at 1pm, effective from Tuesday Nov 3, 2026 and reconfirmed unchanged on Nov 4, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-brightwell-peak-cutoff-1pm]. The idea of a weekly consolidation arrangement for Duraline was confirmed dead on Nov 9, 2026, when Sam Quintero ([[sam]]) was notified and Brightwell's internal records were updated to reflect his new title, Key Accounts Manager [cite:memoryAtom:f-sam-notified-duraline-consolidation-dead].

**Supplier diversification** — Brightwell opened an evaluation of Halvorsen Packaging on Nov 4, 2026 as a possible secondary supplier for corrugated void-fill and carton stock, but nothing is final yet — no RFQ response, pricing, contact, lead time, MOQ, or freight terms have been confirmed pending the quote packet [cite:memoryAtom:f-halvorsen-packaging-evaluation-opened].

**Team and ownership** — Maya Chen ([[maya-chen]]) is the ops lead and workspace owner for Brightwell Supply Co. [cite:memoryAtom:f-maya-chen-ops-lead-owner].

## Agents
- **Ops Assistant** (`ag-ops`) — warehouse, carriers, CL Rollout cutover; orchestrates the readiness cycle; runs the scheduled readiness sweep (06:30 daily d1-d7, 06:30+15:30 d8-d14) · 46 observations
- **Sales Assistant** (`ag-sales`) — accounts, quoting, Vantek renegotiation, Duraline account · 31 observations
- **Finance Assistant** (`ag-finance`) — AP/AR, month close, margin, the confidential Vantek rate memo (visibility agent:ag-finance) · 16 observations
- **Support Assistant** (`ag-support`) — support queue, refunds, daily 08:00 queue digest; DEPRECATED after day 12 (silent d13-d14) · 17 observations
- **Service Desk Assistant** (`ag-servicedesk`) — successor to the Support Assistant: queue digest from day 12, refunds · 14 observations
- **Quality Assistant** (`ag-quality`) — lot capture, LabTrack LIMS, retained-sample testing, cycle counts; specialist role in the readiness cycle · 15 observations
- **Purchasing Assistant** (`ag-purchasing`) — POs, inbound receipts, stock positions, supplier price schedules; specialist role in the readiness cycle · 49 observations
- **Dispatch Digest Agent** (`ag-dispatch`) — scheduled-only: 06:00 daily dispatch digest to Maya and Leo (figures first, <=120 words); specialist role in the readiness cycle · 9 observations
- **Rollout Gate Agent** (`ag-rollout-gate`) — renders READY / NOT READY verdicts on the readiness cycle document; dispatched by the Ops Assistant · 2 observations
- **General Assistant** (`bw2-generalist`) — workspace-visibility probe agent for cases; produces no corpus threads · 0 observations
- **General Assistant** (`bw2-outsider`) — empty-visibility probe agent for permission cases; produces no corpus threads · 0 observations
- **Purchasing Assistant** (`ag-purchasing-copy`) — second copy of the Purchasing Assistant with the identical display name, created by Leo on November 6 while testing agent setup; answered two PO questions and was never used again · 3 observations

pages.title: CL Rollout
pages.summary: CL Rollout is the cutover project migrating warehouse operations from StockPro to NexBin at the Stockton warehouse .
pages.content:
CL Rollout is the cutover project migrating warehouse operations from [[stockpro]] to [[nexbin]] at the [[stockton-warehouse]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-runbook-scope].

## Scope
The CL Rollout cutover runbook (doc "CL Rollout cutover runbook (2026-11-02)") covers only the sequence, timeline, freeze window, rollback criterion, roles, and contacts for the [[nexbin]] cutover at the [[stockton-warehouse]]; it explicitly excludes supplier, finance, or account matters [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-runbook-scope].

## Timeline
The go-live moved to Thursday Nov 12, 2026 at 05:00 (from a prior Wed Nov 11 date), per the Nov 10, 2026 runbook revision, after the final data-migration dry run in nexbin-stage surfaced a bin-mapping error requiring an extra day to fix and re-verify before promoting to production [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-golive-nov12-correction]. This 05:00 Nov 12 time was confirmed per the [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]]; a separately logged working assumption of 04:00 from [[owen]] is not the agreed cutover time and should not be used for planning [cite:memoryAtom:f-golive-time-correction-nov11].

## Readiness Process
The scheduled readiness sweep procedure is: (1) open the current [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]], (2) dispatch Purchasing for the round covering inbound receipts through cutover, (3) collect Purchasing's section plus any pending role updates, (4) reconcile standing-value changes reported that day (cutoffs, contacts, onsite status, lot-capture wording), (5) publish an updated cycle document version, (6) report status to [[maya-chen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-procedure-steps].

As part of runbook prep on Nov 2, 2026, the [[stockpro]] throughput baseline was pulled and found steady with no anomalies, and the [[nexbin]] UAT queue was checked for blocking tickets with none found open [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-baseline-check-episode]. The 15:30 sweep on Nov 9, 2026 (second run under the new twice-daily cadence) found nexbin uat and stage both healthy matching the 06:30 snapshot, no new [[stockpro]] cases, no new purchasing or quality flags, and the [[duraline]] consolidation-plan retraction noted as a non-blocking account-side change; the clean result was reported to [[maya-chen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov9-1530-sweep-clean-pass]. The final PM readiness sweep on day 14 of the cutover cycle (2026-11-15, 15:30) found no open [[nexbin]] incidents, zero carrier/pick exceptions since the 2pm same-day cutoff, normal service desk queue depth, and no open action items in the readiness cycle document; a nothing-to-report note was logged and sent to [[maya-chen]], with no new cycle round opened and no further sweeps scheduled [cite:memoryAtom:f-final-readiness-sweep-pm-nov15].

## Checklist and Rollback Criteria
NexBin Cutover Checklist v3.2 steps 7-8 require a full parallel cycle count in stage (Customer-owned, step 7) feeding into reconciling parallel count variance to zero (Partner-owned, step 8) before cutover; this pairing was not reflected in the CL Rollout cutover runbook as of Nov 6, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-parallel-cycle-count-gap]. As of that date, vendor confirmation from [[nexbin]] on checklist steps 12-13 (scheduling vendor case queue coverage for cutover day and confirming the rollback environment snapshot) remained pending and could not be self-certified [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-vendor-confirmation-pending-steps-12-13].

Per NexBin Cutover Checklist v3.3 (mirrored Nov 12, 2026), rollback trigger steps renumbered due to insertion of a new pre-cutover step 11; rollback must now be initiated if go-live validation fails at step 18 (was step 17), or if post-cutover reconciliation variance at step 23 exceeds 2% of counted SKU lines, with the 2% threshold and 4-hour reconciliation timing otherwise unchanged from v3.2 [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-v33-rollback-step-renumbering]. The new step 11, owned by Brightwell (Customer), freezes inbound receipts at 12:00 the day before cutover to lock counted stock levels and reduce reconciliation variance at go-live, matching wording Purchasing had already logged independently [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-v33-freeze-inbound-receipts-step].

## Data Reconciliation
A full inbound receipts reconciliation run on Nov 6, 2026 between the [[nexbin]] export and [[stockpro]] receipts log across all zones since go-live prep started covered 2,522 NexBin lines vs 1,976 StockPro lines, finding 356 mismatches (about 14%): 210 quantity variances under 5 units, 98 timing offsets where NexBin logged a receipt a day later than StockPro, and 48 lines present only in NexBin from parallel cutover test activity. 22 mismatches were adhesive-category lines with no unusual pattern; no corrective action was taken and the full mismatch list was exported for review [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-stockpro-reconciliation-nov2026]. During that pull, the NexBin inbound receipts export repeatedly timed out and returned 502 errors on [[zone-d]] and zone E pages under heavy load, requiring 2-3 retries per page [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-export-zone-timeout-under-load].

On Nov 9, 2026, an EDI 856 replay of 812 pending ASN records pulled from [[stockpro]] against nexbin-uat resulted in 761 accepted, 4 malformed-segment rejects, and 50 records in batch 3 unresolved after 40 consecutive failed retries; the same batch 3 payload succeeded immediately against nexbin-stage, confirming the payload was well-formed and the failure was localized to nexbin-uat under load — this does not confirm nexbin-uat capacity is adequate and says nothing about production behavior. Retries were stopped on user instruction, leaving batch 3 for review after lunch [cite:memoryAtom:f-edi-856-replay-nov9-nexbin-uat].

## Zone Rollout
As of Nov 8, 2026, [[maya-chen]] abandoned the '[[zone-b]] migration draft' document, leaving most sections as placeholders, and worked directly in the CL Rollout runbook instead; the draft should not be used as a current source of [[zone-b]]/CL Rollout status [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-b-migration-draft-abandoned]. As of Nov 12, 2026, the nexbin-stage environment was torn down and cleared (confirmed by [[owen]]) and made free for the next zone's dry run, with [[zone-d]]'s dry run beginning immediately after under [[owen]]'s observation [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-stage-cleared-zone-d-dryrun].

## Related Holds
The Q4 Carrier RFP draft is being kept as an internal working draft only, not to be sent or distributed until the user explicitly approves; this hold, set 2026-11-05, is expected to last until after the CL Rollout cutover is past [cite:memoryAtom:f-q4-carrier-rfp-hold-no-distribution]. [[duraline]]'s weekly consolidation plan, active since Nov 4, 2026, was retracted as of the Nov 9, 2026 06:30 readiness sweep, leaving no active or replacement schedule [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-consolidation-plan-retracted].

## People
[[owen]] remains reachable by phone and screen-share during the cutover window and continues to be onsite Tuesdays and Thursdays until cutover, but is remote (not onsite as he had earlier said) for the go-live at the [[stockton-warehouse]] since his travel plans fell through [cite:memoryAtom:f-owen-hallberg-remote-golive-correction].

## Disputed

**Owen's paging cadence vs. digest inclusion:** One record states [[owen]] should only be paged on his onsite days, Tuesday and Thursday, for CL Rollout / NexBin cutover support, per his own request [cite:memoryAtom:f-owen-hallberg-paging-preference]. Another record states [[owen]] was added as a recipient of the daily [[dispatch-digest-agent]] Dispatch Digest, alongside standard recipients Maya and [[leo]], through the duration of the CL Rollout cutover so dispatch delays aren't mistaken for NexBin integration errors, [[receiving]] the standard figures-first digest daily with no added WMS detail, to be dropped once the cutover period ends [cite:memoryAtom:f-dispatch-digest-owen-added]. These two records are not reconciled.

**Reason for holding the [[zone-c]] flip:** One record states [[zone-c]]'s live flip to NexBin production was intentionally held back until Nov 13, 2026 (the day after [[zone-b]] went live) per [[owen]]'s explicit instruction on Nov 12, 2026, so only one zone change per day lands for floor leads to track, even though the [[zone-c]] diff was already clean [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-c-live-flip-held-nov13]. Another record states that on Nov 12, 2026, [[zone-c]]'s location diff initially showed 3 mismatches in aisle 14 from stale bin renumbering (fixed source-side by [[owen]]), and that on re-run the diff came back clean (1,140/1,140 matched), but [[maya-chen]] chose to hold the [[zone-c]] live flip until Nov 13, 2026 despite the clean diff [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-c-diff-clean-flip-held]. These two records disagree on who made the hold decision and attribute a different rationale.

See also: [[nexbin]], [[stockpro]], [[maya-chen]], [[owen]], [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]], [[stockton-warehouse]], [[zone-b]], [[zone-c]], [[zone-d]], [[dispatch-digest-agent]]

pages.content:
## Overview
The CL Rollout Readiness Cycle Document is the living reference document used to track readiness for the [[cl-rollout]] cutover, including scheduled sweep procedures, standing-value updates, and status reporting [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-procedure-steps].

## Sweep Procedure
The scheduled readiness sweep procedure defined in the document consists of six steps: (1) open the current CL Rollout readiness cycle document, (2) dispatch Purchasing for the round covering inbound receipts through cutover, (3) collect Purchasing's section plus any pending role updates, (4) reconcile standing-value changes reported that day (cutoffs, contacts, onsite status, lot-capture wording), (5) publish an updated cycle document version, and (6) report status to [[maya-chen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-procedure-steps].

## Go-Live Time
The confirmed CL Rollout go-live time recorded in the readiness cycle document is Thursday Nov 12, 2026 at 05:00 [cite:memoryAtom:f-golive-time-correction-nov11]. [[owen]]'s separately logged working assumption of 04:00 is not the agreed cutover time and should not be used for planning [cite:memoryAtom:f-golive-time-correction-nov11].

## Scope Boundaries
Per instruction issued 2026-11-13 regarding a door 2 roller jam, temporary operational issues such as a short-term dock or equipment outage with a known fix date are to be noted only in the relevant sweep report, not added to the readiness cycle document or other SOP documents [cite:memoryAtom:f-temporary-dock-issues-not-in-runbook].

## Sweep History
On 2026-11-09 at 15:30, the second sweep of the day under the new twice-daily cadence found [[nexbin]] uat and stage both healthy matching the 06:30 snapshot, no new [[stockpro]] cases, no new purchasing or quality flags, and the [[duraline]] consolidation-plan retraction noted as a non-blocking account-side change; no changes were made to the readiness cycle document and the clean result was reported to [[maya-chen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov9-1530-sweep-clean-pass].

On Thursday Nov 12, 2026 at 06:00, the [[dispatch-digest-agent]] ran the scheduled dispatch digest, reporting 38 pallets staged overnight across outbound lanes (34 wrapped/labeled, 4 awaiting label print), 0 holds flagged, and 3 confirmed carrier pickups (09:00 regional LTL, 12:30 will-call for two local accounts, 16:00 line-haul consolidation) with no reschedules or cancellations, and no leftover pallets from the prior day's line-haul; the digest was sent to Maya and [[leo]], and since no blocking issue was found, no update was made to the readiness cycle document [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov12-dispatch-digest-episode].

On 2026-11-15 at 15:30, the final PM readiness sweep for day 14 of the CL Rollout cutover cycle found no open incidents on NexBin, zero carrier/pick exceptions since the 2pm same-day cutoff, normal service desk queue depth, and no open action items in the readiness cycle document; a nothing-to-report note was logged and sent to Maya Chen, no new cycle round was opened, and no further sweeps were scheduled [cite:memoryAtom:f-final-readiness-sweep-pm-nov15].

See also: [[cl-rollout]], [[maya-chen]], [[nexbin]], [[dispatch-digest-agent]], [[owen]]

pages.content:
## Overview
The Dispatch Digest Agent is the system responsible for producing the daily dispatch digest covering shipments dispatched, pallets staged, carrier delays, and open dispatch exceptions [cite:memoryAtom:f-dispatch-digest-format-rule]. It also performs a post-send carrier manifest reconciliation step [cite:memoryAtom:f-carrier-manifest-reconciliation-rule].

## Daily Digest Format
The digest must lead with figures first — shipments dispatched, pallets staged, carrier delays, and open dispatch exceptions — with no preamble, followed by one short prose paragraph of context or callouts without bullets, and the whole digest must stay under 120 words total; if it runs over length, the paragraph is cut rather than the figures [cite:memoryAtom:f-dispatch-digest-format-rule].

## Document Update Policy
The agent only updates a document as part of the daily dispatch digest process when an exception is found in overnight staging or carrier pickup data; on routine days with no exceptions, it sends the figures-first digest but makes no document update [cite:memoryAtom:f-dispatch-digest-no-doc-update-on-routine-day]. This was borne out on Nov 12 2026, when no blocking issue was found and no update was made to the readiness cycle document, matching [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov12-dispatch-digest-episode].

## Recipients
Standard recipients of the daily digest are [[maya-chen]] and [[leo]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov12-dispatch-digest-episode] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov15-dispatch-digest-episode]. [[owen]] Hallberg was added as a recipient alongside the standard recipients through the duration of the [[cl-rollout]] cutover (added Nov 10, 2026) so that dispatch delays aren't mistaken for [[nexbin]] integration errors; his copy is the same standard figures-first digest with no added WMS detail, and he is intended to be dropped from the list once the cutover period ends [cite:memoryAtom:f-dispatch-digest-owen-added].

## Carrier Manifest Reconciliation
After sending the daily dispatch digest, the agent pulls a carrier manifest export (roughly 500 rows across carriers, paginated 100 rows per page) and reconciles it against staged/dispatched counts as a post-send step [cite:memoryAtom:f-carrier-manifest-reconciliation-rule].

## Notable Episodes

### Nov 10, 2026 — Duplicate Digest Run
Two separate scheduled dispatch digest runs occurred for the same date under the same 06:00 daily schedule label: one thread (D-digest-dispatch-09) produced a pallet-focused digest, and another (D-dump-disp-09, logged starting 07:00) produced a different outbound-count digest with an added manifest reconciliation step, resulting in two distinct digests sent to [[maya-chen]] and [[leo]] the same day [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov10-duplicate-digest-run-anomaly].

### Nov 10, 2026 — Reconciliation Failure
During the Nov 10 2026 post-digest carrier manifest reconciliation, the second carrier's export returned malformed/truncated JSON around rows 400-450 on three consecutive attempts (including reduced page sizes); the segment was aborted rather than reported, leaving roughly 400 of 500 total rows confirmed clean with no mismatches, and the failed segment was scheduled to retry on the next cycle [cite:memoryAtom:f-carrier-manifest-reconciliation-failure-nov10].

### Nov 12, 2026 — Routine Digest
At 06:00, the agent reported 38 pallets staged overnight across outbound lanes (34 wrapped/labeled, 4 awaiting label print) and 0 holds flagged; 3 carrier pickups scheduled (09:00 regional LTL, 12:30 will-call for two local accounts, 16:00 line-haul consolidation) were all confirmed on the carrier portal with no reschedules or cancellations, and no leftover pallets remained from the prior day's line-haul. The digest was sent to [[maya-chen]] and [[leo]] with no document update [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov12-dispatch-digest-episode].

### Nov 14, 2026 — Reconciliation Episode
In thread D-dump-disp-13, 480 rows across 5 carriers were checked in batches of 100: batch 2 hit a timeout at row 148 and succeeded on retry, batch 4 returned a 502 server error and succeeded on retry, and batch 3 (rows 201-300) found one blank weight field on a carrier manifest line, logged for carrier follow-up but not treated as a dispatch exception. Total reconciled: 480 manifest rows consistent with 214 pallets and 61 orders from the digest [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov14-manifest-reconciliation-episode].

### Nov 15, 2026 — Quiet Sunday Digest
At 06:00, the agent reported 10 pallets staged overnight (Dock 1: 6, Dock 2: 4, Dock 3 closed for the morning), two confirmed standard LTL carrier pickups (07:00 and 09:30) with no will-call pickups, and no exceptions found. The digest was delivered to [[maya-chen]] and [[leo]] describing a quiet Sunday morning with nothing further to report [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov15-dispatch-digest-episode].

## Disputed
The record of [[owen]] Hallberg's addition as a digest recipient during the [[cl-rollout]] cutover is flagged as an unresolved conflict (CONFLICT-CARDED) in the fact store; the fact store provides no additional side or resolution beyond the recorded addition and its stated intent that he be dropped once the cutover ends [cite:memoryAtom:f-dispatch-digest-owen-added].

See also: [[maya-chen]], [[leo]], [[owen]], [[cl-rollout]], [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]], [[nexbin]]

Also known as: DuraLite, DuraLite Fasteners

## Overview

DuraLite is a small, separate account distinct from [[duraline-industrial-supply]] (also referred to as [[duraline]]) [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-prepay-only-terms] [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-fasteners-modesto-location]. Operating as DuraLite Fasteners, it is based out of Modesto and carries orders such as assorted hex bolts and washers under standard freight terms, with no Duraline-specific handling applied [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-fasteners-modesto-location].

## Account Terms

DuraLite's account record confirms it has no credit line or net payment terms on file — it is prepay-only, meaning any order must be paid in full before release [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-prepay-only-terms].

## Prepay Flag History

DuraLite's account previously carried a prepay flag set to true from an earlier hold with no linked reason code [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-prepay-flag-cleared]. On 2026-11-14, the [[service-desk-assistant]] cleared this flag after finding no unpaid or disputed orders and no active refund tied to it in the current window, logging the reason "cleared during handover cleanup, no open balance found" on the account record [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-prepay-flag-cleared].

## Current Order Status

As of Nov 14, 2026, a DuraLite Fasteners order for assorted hex bolts and washers (placed the prior Thursday) was in "picked and staged" status with no carrier scan yet logged. It was staged for outbound ahead of the 2pm same-day cutoff, with no holds or backorder flags, under standard freight terms [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-hexbolt-order-staged-nov14].

## Disputed

There is an unresolved conflict regarding authority over DuraLite's prepay flag and how it should be handled:

- One position holds that clearing an account's prepay flag, such as DuraLite's, is outside the support role's scope, and that only someone with AP (accounts payable) authority can clear or confirm it [cite:memoryAtom:f-prepay-flag-clearing-authority].
- Relatedly, [[tessa-nguyen]] wanted open items — including the DuraLite prepay flag — logged precisely (exact macro names, ledger status, next-action owner) in the handover doc without the Support Assistant taking action itself, explicitly not touching the flag but logging it clean for whoever picks it up [cite:memoryAtom:f-tessa-handover-logging-preference].
- Contrary to both positions, the [[service-desk-assistant]] did in fact clear the DuraLite prepay flag on 2026-11-14, after determining there was no open balance [cite:memoryAtom:f-duralite-prepay-flag-cleared].

This page does not resolve which position governs; all sides are recorded as given.

See also: [[duraline-industrial-supply]], [[duraline]], [[service-desk-assistant]], [[tessa-nguyen]]

pages.content:
Duraline is a customer account of Brightwell Supply Co., ranked as one of the company's top-3 accounts [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-top3-account].

## Account Management

The account is handled by [[jonas]] (Jonas Solheim), who serves as sales lead and is also responsible for the Vantek renegotiation [cite:memoryAtom:f-jonas-solheim-sales-lead-role]. As of 2026-11-15, Duraline's interim point of contact is Kwame Asante, effective through November 30, as flagged in a Callouts note included in the Sunday [[support-queue-digest]] sent by the [[service-desk-assistant]] to [[maya-chen]], [[tessa-nguyen]], and [[jonas]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-15].

## Dock Hours and Delivery Conventions

For questions about Duraline's dock hours or delivery conventions, the [[service-desk-assistant]] treats the Duraline account playbook (v4) as the system of record, cross-referencing Jonas's notes for any supersession before quoting a figure. As of 2026-11-15, both sources are in agreement with no conflict [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-dock-hours-verification].

## Incidents

On 2026-11-04, a user asked Support Assistant to draft a short Duraline apology for a late shipment, but the user cancelled before drafting began, saying the apology would instead be sent from the sales side; no draft was produced or sent [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-apology-draft-aborted].

On 2026-11-06, a Duraline order was short-shipped, with only 8 of 12 cases arriving. This incident prompted the addition of a new SHORT refund reason code to the refund-memo tool and to the [[refund-memo-procedure]] document [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-short-shipment-incident].

## QA Hold

The Duraline adhesive QA hold was narrowed on 2026-11-11 to apply only to [[vantek-adhesives]] lots before lot VA-2618, rather than functioning as a blanket hold on all Duraline shipments as previously recorded [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-qa-hold-narrowed].

## Same-Day Pilot Route

Route M-7, a same-day pilot test route for Duraline, was dropped entirely on 2026-11-11 per the user's instruction, being described as a test that would not go forward, and was removed from carrier routing notes [cite:memoryAtom:f-route-m7-cancelled].

See also: [[jonas]], [[vantek-adhesives]], [[refund-memo-procedure]], [[service-desk-assistant]], [[priya-rao]]

pages.title: Duraline Industrial Supply
pages.summary: Duraline Industrial Supply is a Brightwell customer account, distinct from the smaller, prepay-only account DuraLite (no credit line or net terms on file) .
pages.content:
## Overview

[[duraline]] Industrial Supply is a Brightwell customer account, distinct from the smaller, prepay-only account [[duralite]] (no credit line or net terms on file) [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-prepay-only-terms]. Since Nov 9, 2026 (set after a naming shortcut recurred a third time), the account name must always be written in full as "Duraline Industrial Supply," never abbreviated, in every mention including internal notes [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-full-name-only-rule].

## Contacts

Primary contact is Renee Alvarez [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-order-78104-confirmed-compliant]. As of Nov 15, 2026 she is out until Nov 30, 2026, with Kwame Asante as interim primary contact; she remains the contact to revert to on return [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-interim-contact-kwame-asante]. [[jonas]] (Jonas Solheim) flagged the contact field as a recurring error (previously misattributed to Tom Iverson) and instructed it be double-checked whenever the Duraline playbook is opened [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-contact-recurring-error-check].

## Standing Account Rules

- Any missed same-day cutoff must be flagged to [[jonas]] the same day, not the next morning, no exceptions — set after the PO 77812 cutoff-miss escalation (Nov 4, 2026), overriding any default next-morning/batched cadence [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-cutoff-same-day-flag-rule].
- Figures-first format (numbers before narrative) is the default for any future note or communication to this account, not just a one-off apology [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-figures-first-default].
- For updates to [[sam]] (Sam Quintero) about this account, numbers must come first, context after [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-figures-first-reporting-preference].
- Every Duraline order must have a PO number attached before release — a hard requirement in the account playbook, under the exception cutoff line [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-po-required-before-release].
- Starting Nov 13, 2026, every order confirmation must cite Duraline's PO number, no exceptions, set by [[jonas]] after order 78104 was checked and already met this via Renee Alvarez's account and the confirmation template's required-field enforcement [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-po-confirmation-citation-rule].
- Order 78104 (Renee Alvarez's account, received 11:20am, within the 1:30pm exception cutoff) was confirmed Nov 13, 2026 to already carry the required PO number [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-order-78104-confirmed-compliant].

## Logistics: Dock Hours and Cutoffs

[[receiving]] dock hours are 06:00–14:00, per info received the week of Nov 14, 2026, for use when scheduling deliveries [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-dock-hours]. Orders received before 1pm ship same day regardless of peak season, with a confirmed account-specific exception cutoff of 1:30pm, distinct from the general peak same-day cutoff [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-order-cutoff-130pm]. The general (non-Duraline) peak-season same-day cutoff moved to 2:00pm as of Jonas Solheim's Nov 15, 2026 update, separate from Duraline's 1:30pm exception [cite:memoryAtom:f-peak-same-day-cutoff-2pm]. The dock closes at 13:00 on Fridays regardless of playbook text — an authoritative standing rule set by [[jonas]] on Nov 14, 2026 (repeated twice after being dropped from the draft), holding even if a future playbook edit garbles or removes the Friday line [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-friday-dock-close-1pm-rule].

## Q3 2026 Supplier Scorecard

On-time delivery: 91.2% (target 95%); fill rate: 98.4% (target 97%). Three late-shipment incidents: PO 76210 (4 days late), PO 76988 (5 days late), PO 77401 (7 days late). PO 77812 (the Nov 4, 2026 incident) is not among these, having occurred later [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-q3-2026-scorecard-kpis].

## PO 77812 Incident and Fee Policy

There is no standing policy waiving Brightwell's $150 expedite fee for Duraline late shipments. The Nov 4, 2026 waiver on PO 77812 (the third late-cutoff incident that quarter) was a one-time exception overriding the fee-scoring model; a recurrence (e.g., a fourth incident) requires an actual policy rather than another one-off waiver [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-expedite-fee-no-standing-waiver].

## Support and QA

Sam Quintero's support queue handover to [[tessa-nguyen]] (Nov 8, 2026) distinguishes a Duraline adhesive QA hold from a standard refund hold — different hold types not to be conflated in ticket processing [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-qa-hold-vs-refund-hold]. The GripLoc 275 restock under PO 78120 (Vantek SO-114872) uses lots VA-2640–VA-2644, one lot per pallet across 5 pallets (pallet 1=VA-2640 … pallet 5=VA-2644); all five lots fall outside the QA hold [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-78120-lots-outside-qa-hold].

## Sales Pipeline and Products

Quote Q-4471 closed at the standard restock quantity, no outstanding TBD, per Jonas Solheim's sales weekly pipeline revision dated Nov 15, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-q4471-closed]. A proposed move to weekly consolidated shipments (earlier raised by Renee Alvarez as planned/pending) was declined by Duraline; the pending note was retracted from the account brief per Jonas Solheim's Nov 9, 2026 update [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-consolidation-declined]. On Nov 9, 2026, the Sales Assistant confirmed to [[sam]] (Sam Quintero) that the consolidation idea is dead [cite:memoryAtom:f-sam-notified-duraline-consolidation-dead].

For a [[griploc-275]] add-on, [[jonas]] is quoting Duraline (Renee Alvarez) a 5-business-day lead time from PO to Brightwell's dock, per Dana Nwosu's email on [[vantek-adhesives]] logistics — standard, no expedite needed unless told otherwise [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-vantek-lead-time].

## Additional Notes

On Nov 4, 2026, a full CRM pipeline export of all ~300 open opportunities was completed across 6 pages for Jonas Solheim; pages 3, 5, and 6 hit transient errors (a 502 timeout, a permissions/403 error) [cite:memoryAtom:f-crm-pipeline-export-nov4-2026]. Sam wants the Sales Assistant to never paste links to CRM quotes, docs, or records — instead give the quote number or account name directly, re-fetching fresh from the CRM each time [cite:memoryAtom:f-no-links-give-numbers-preference].

See also: [[jonas]], [[sam]], [[vantek-adhesives]], [[griploc-275]], [[duralite]], [[tessa-nguyen]]

pages.title: GripLoc 275
pages.summary: GripLoc 275 is a threadlocker product supplied by Vantek Adhesives.
pages.content:
## Overview

GripLoc 275 is a threadlocker product supplied by [[vantek-adhesives]]. Per Vantek's product page (mirrored Nov 8, 2026), it has a viscosity of 1200-1800 cP at 25°C, a service temperature range of -54°C to 149°C, a cure time of 24 hours to full strength at room temperature (with functional handling strength reached in 30-45 minutes), and is available in pack sizes of 10 ml, 50 ml, and 250 ml [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc275-specifications]. It has a shelf life of 18 months unopened, per Vantek's product page as reflected in the Vantek Adhesives account brief [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc275-shelf-life]. GripLoc 275 replaces GripLoc 271 across all Vantek catalog listings and distributor price schedules; customers currently specifying GripLoc 271 should transition new orders to GripLoc 275, as formulation and application guidance for both products is substantially similar [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc275-replaces-griploc271]. GripLoc 275's case pack is 24 units per case, per the item master and price schedule v2; this pack size is standard and applies to [[duraline-industrial-supply]] orders as well, with no [[duraline]]-specific override [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-case-pack].

## Supply and Ordering

GripLoc 275 is sourced from [[vantek-adhesives]]. If a reorder triggers before November 8, 2026, Vantek's 40-case-per-PO allocation cap still applies, so a peak-season top-up above 40 cases must be split across multiple POs; the cap lifts from November 9, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-peak-topup-cap-split]. GripLoc 275's reorder point was lowered from 90 cases to 75 cases effective November 11, 2026, per [[leo]] Kirkwood, because peak season demand was settling and 90 was leaving too much stock sitting; the open-PO/inbound schedule threshold and PO suggestion logic use 75 cases from this date forward [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-griploc-275-reorder-point-75-nov11].

On PO-2026-4466 (30 cases), Vantek pushed the due date from Friday, November 6, 2026 to Tuesday, November 10, 2026; [[jonas]] Solheim and [[maya-chen]] were notified, and the ERP due date was updated accordingly [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4466-date-push]. PO-2026-1174 (40 cases) shipped November 6, 2026 on one-way pallets per its ASN, with the open-PO tracker updated to show receipt expected around November 10, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-1174-shipped-nov6]. Due to a shortage of returnable pallets, Vantek is shipping GripLoc 275 orders on one-way pallets until its pallet pool recovers, and Brightwell's dock breaks the pallets down and scraps them rather than returning them to Vantek [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-griploc275-one-way-pallets].

During a cutover-related PO review on 2026-11-09 covering 22 open POs (PO-1180 through PO-1201) due Nov 11 through Nov 13, the review was paused at 14 of 22 when the user was called away. PO-1183, a Vantek GripLoc 275 restock of 5 pallets, was expedited to land Tuesday Nov 10, alongside PO-1185, PO-1188, PO-1190, and PO-1191; other POs were deferred to after cutover or left untagged [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov9-2026-cutover-po-review-paused-14-of-22].

A one-page receiving plan document titled 'GripLoc 275 restock — receiving plan' (version 1) was created on 2026-11-12 for [[receiving]], built from Vantek's order acknowledgment against the GripLoc 275 PO raised November 11, 2026. It includes Vantek's order reference tied to Brightwell's PO, ship date, freight mode, arrival window, pallet count, lot range, and a five-line receiving checklist; no dock door was assigned since door assignments come from dispatch on the day [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-receiving-plan-doc-created].

## Quality and Lots

The GripLoc 275 restock under PO 78120 (Vantek SO-114872) uses lots VA-2640 through VA-2644, one lot per pallet across 5 pallets. All five lots fall after the VA-2618 boundary, so none of this restock is subject to the [[duraline-industrial-supply]] adhesive QA hold [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-78120-lots-outside-qa-hold].

A spot-check on 2026-11-13 compared 20 of 92 GripLoc 275 rows from the [[nexbin]] export against [[stockpro]] bin records: 17 matched exactly, and 3 showed small variances of a few units, attributed to picks logged between the export windows rather than a real discrepancy [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc275-spotcheck-nov13].

## Pricing

[[maya-chen]]'s? — For Meridian Fabricators, open quote Q-4472 for GripLoc 275 remains pending; a Vantek price schedule update raises GripLoc 275 to $15.10/unit effective Dec 1, 2026, and the current quote holds at the prior price until then, per [[jonas]] Solheim's Nov 15, 2026 sales pipeline update [cite:memoryAtom:f-meridian-griploc275-price-update-dec1].

## Disputed

There is an unresolved conflict regarding GripLoc 275's lead time from [[vantek-adhesives]]. Per Dana Nwosu's email to [[jonas]] Solheim on Nov 11, 2026, the lead time is 5 business days from PO to Brightwell's dock, standard with no expedite needed; this figure is recorded in the Vantek Adhesives account notes under logistics. However, this figure is the rep's by email and is not stated on the Vantek 2027 price schedule, and terms, rebate status, and pricing sections were left untouched. Jonas is quoting this 5-business-day figure to [[duraline-industrial-supply]] (Renee Alvarez) for the GripLoc 275 add-on unless told otherwise [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-vantek-lead-time].

pages.title: Jonas Solheim
pages.summary: Jonas Solheim is the sales lead, handling the Vantek Adhesives renegotiation and the Duraline Industrial Supply account .
pages.content:
Jonas Solheim is the sales lead, handling the [[vantek-adhesives]] renegotiation and the [[duraline-industrial-supply]] account [cite:memoryAtom:f-jonas-solheim-sales-lead-role].

## Vantek Adhesives Account

Jonas can release [[vantek-adhesives]] purchase orders when [[leo]] is out, since he knows the account; this is recorded on the purchasing page [cite:memoryAtom:f-jonas-vantek-po-backup]. He was notified when Vantek Adhesives pushed the due date on PO-2026-4466 ([[griploc-275]], 30 cases) from Friday, November 6, 2026 to Tuesday, November 10, 2026, alongside [[maya-chen]], with the ERP updated accordingly [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4466-date-push]. He was also notified of PO-2026-4489's due date moving up from November 13 to November 11, 2026 after early vendor delivery confirmation, since he had a backorder pending release on that PO [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4489-early-delivery-date-change], and of PO-2026-4512's due date push from November 16 to November 19, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4512-date-push].

Per his Nov 10, 2026 account brief correction, the 4% Vantek volume rebate was never agreed by Vantek — it was only Brightwell's internal proposal, not signed off by Dana Nwosu — and it must be treated as not agreed until further notice: not quoted, not mentioned to customers, and not built into margin projections, superseding the earlier "pending paperwork" status [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-rebate-not-agreed-correction]. Separately, when Vantek remittance or payment-method changes are learned by Finance, they are saved as a Finance-only memory and not restated in the Vantek account brief, since that brief is Jonas's document [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-remittance-not-in-account-brief].

## [[duraline]] Industrial Supply Account

Jonas set a standing rule on Nov 4, 2026 that any missed same-day cutoff on the [[duraline-industrial-supply]] account must be flagged to him the same day it happens, not the next morning, with no exceptions, overriding any default batched or next-morning reporting cadence [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-cutoff-same-day-flag-rule]. He flagged the account's contact field as a recurring error (previously misattributed to Tom Iverson) and instructed double-checking it whenever the Duraline playbook is opened [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-contact-recurring-error-check]. Starting Nov 13, 2026, he set the standing rule that every Duraline order confirmation must cite Duraline's PO number, with no exceptions [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-po-confirmation-citation-rule]. He also set the authoritative rule, repeated twice, that Duraline's [[receiving]] dock closes at 13:00 on Fridays regardless of what the playbook text says, holding even if a future playbook edit drops the exception [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-friday-dock-close-1pm-rule]. As of Nov 15, 2026, the [[duraline-industrial-supply]] playbook (v4) and Jonas's notes agree on dock hours with no conflict [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-dock-hours-verification]. Per his Nov 15, 2026 sales pipeline revision, Duraline's quote Q-4471 closed at the standard restock quantity with no outstanding TBD [cite:memoryAtom:f-duraline-q4471-closed].

## Sales Pipeline and Reports

Jonas's sales weekly pipeline document contains working/rolling figures for open quotes that are explicitly not to be quoted to customers yet, as of the week of Nov 2, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-sales-pipeline-figures-not-final]. On Nov 4, 2026, a full CRM pipeline export of all ~300 open opportunities was completed for him across 6 pages, with transient errors on three pages resolved on retry and Duraline-tagged rows confirmed clean [cite:memoryAtom:f-crm-pipeline-export-nov4-2026]. He stated explicitly that CRM pipeline exports must be done in full before any filtering is applied — always export the complete dataset first, then filter afterward [cite:memoryAtom:f-export-before-filter-preference].

His pipeline movement report for eight named small accounts, comparing Q3 2026 vs Q4-to-date, was completed Nov 9, 2026 as a 5-tab spreadsheet with a summary tab first and movers ranked by absolute percent change, delivered at sheets/pipeline-review-q3-vs-q4td-2026-r2 [cite:memoryAtom:f-jonas-pipeline-q3-q4td-report-episode]. In these reports, Baymont Rail must always be included as a row for completeness but must never be ranked as a mover, regardless of its actual movement [cite:memoryAtom:f-baymont-rail-report-inclusion-rule].

Per his Nov 15, 2026 sales pipeline update, Meridian Fabricators' open quote Q-4472 for [[griploc-275]] remains pending; a Vantek price schedule update raises GripLoc 275 to $15.10/unit effective Dec 1, 2026, with the current quote held at the prior price until then [cite:memoryAtom:f-meridian-griploc275-price-update-dec1]. Also per that update, the Reno-area sales lead is deferred to next quarter with no approval attached, and Jonas has repeatedly had to correct people who called it approved [cite:memoryAtom:f-reno-lead-deferred-not-approved].

## Documents and Digests

The "Peak same-day cutoff notice" document (created 2026-11-03) is being held as an internal reference only and must not be distributed to support, carriers, or customers until Jonas has reviewed the wording [cite:memoryAtom:f-peak-cutoff-notice-hold]. Despite a Nov 6, 2026 request that the new SHORT refund reason code be flagged in the Nov 7 08:00 [[support-queue-digest]] for Maya and Jonas, the actual digest's Callouts section read "none" and omitted it [cite:memoryAtom:f-short-code-flag-omitted-2026-11-07].

Jonas is on the recipient list for the [[support-queue-digest]], alongside [[maya-chen]] and [[tessa-nguyen]], as reflected in the Nov 10 [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-10], Nov 11 [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-11], Nov 14 [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-14], and Nov 15 [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-15] digest runs; the Nov 15 digest also carried a Callouts note flagging Duraline's interim contact as Kwame Asante through November 30 [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-15]. The digest format was revised to version 2 on Nov 13, 2026, keeping the Callouts heading, a 150-word budget, and the same recipient list of Maya Chen, Tessa Nguyen, and Jonas [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-format-v2]. The [[service-desk-assistant]] sent its first digest under this handoff on Nov 13, 2026 to the same three recipients within the word budget, with delivery confirmed for all [cite:memoryAtom:f-first-digest-run-2026-11-13].

## Disputed

Regarding [[griploc-275]] lead time from [[vantek-adhesives]]: per Dana Nwosu's email to Jonas on Nov 11, 2026, the lead time is 5 business days from PO to Brightwell's dock, standard with no expedite needed. This figure is the rep's by email and is not stated on the Vantek 2027 price schedule; it was recorded in the Vantek account notes under logistics only, leaving terms, rebate status, and pricing sections untouched. Jonas is quoting this figure to [[duraline-industrial-supply]] (Renee Alvarez) for the GripLoc 275 add-on unless told otherwise, but the conflict between the emailed figure and the absence of a corresponding price-schedule statement remains unresolved [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc-275-vantek-lead-time].

See also: [[vantek-adhesives]], [[duraline-industrial-supply]], [[maya-chen]], [[leo]], [[griploc-275]], [[support-queue-digest]], [[service-desk-assistant]], [[tessa-nguyen]]

pages.title: LabTrack LIMS
pages.summary: LabTrack LIMS is the laboratory information management system used for lot tracking, retained-sample recordkeeping, and incoming-inspection workflows, and is referred to informally as "LabTrack" .
pages.content:
Also known as: LabTrack

## Overview

LabTrack LIMS is the laboratory information management system used for lot tracking, retained-sample recordkeeping, and incoming-inspection workflows, and is referred to informally as "LabTrack" [cite:memoryAtom:f-labtrack-location-ref-mapping][cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-restock-shear-gate]. Its export cheat sheet has been revised to version 3, which lists `/exports/v2/lots` as the current export path and warns that the deprecated `/exports/lots` path returns an empty file with no error; version 3 is the one to distribute going forward, and the old path should be removed from bookmarks or scripts [cite:memoryAtom:f-labtrack-cheatsheet-v3-update].

## Export Configuration and Data Semantics

The LabTrack export column `location_ref`, which newly appeared the week of Nov 9, 2026, maps to the LabTrack-internal storage bin rather than the [[nexbin]] bin location, so it should not be assumed to line up with NexBin location codes until a mapping is confirmed; a blank `location_ref` means the lot has not had a putaway scan recorded in LabTrack yet, not necessarily a data gap [cite:memoryAtom:f-labtrack-location-ref-mapping].

For LabTrack retained-sample sweep exports, the lot filter parameter must be set to `ALL` — any other setting silently drops open lots — and `include_archived` must be set to `false`, since setting it `true` causes archived bins to be double-counted and skews pre-cutoff [[vantek-adhesives]] counts [cite:memoryAtom:f-labtrack-retained-sample-export-config].

LabTrack throttles concurrent paging sessions to a maximum of two. In a multi-zone sweep with three or more zone-paging subagents (e.g., Zone A, [[zone-b]], [[zone-c]]/[[zone-d]]), the third subagent cannot start until one of the first two finishes and frees a paging slot, so extra passes must be queued rather than dispatched simultaneously [cite:memoryAtom:f-labtrack-paging-concurrency-limit].

## Known Data Quirks

A LabTrack lot record that spans two result pages during paged export retrieval can cause fields like retention date to silently fail to page through; this caused 2 of 3 Zone A false-positive missing-retention-date flags and the Zone C/D truncated-batch issue in the Nov 13, 2026 retained-sample sweep, both resolved by retrying the specific affected page rather than the whole subagent run [cite:memoryAtom:f-lot-paging-page-split-quirk]. Concretely, on 2026-11-13 the Zone C/D LabTrack paging sweep initially showed 176 lots with 29 retained samples due to a truncated result page; retrying that specific page recovered the missing records, bringing the retained-sample count up to 31 [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-cd-truncated-page-recovery-nov13].

## Zone Coverage for Cycle-Count Sweeps

The weekly cycle-count sweep's LabTrack export covers 6 zone rows: Zone A, [[zone-b]], [[zone-c]], [[zone-d]], [[receiving]], and the Adhesives Cage — not just Zones A through D [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-zone-scope-includes-receiving-adhesives-cage].

## Vantek Adhesive Incoming Inspection Workflow

For [[vantek-adhesives]] restock lots arriving from the week of 2026-11-13 onward, one tube per lot is pulled at the dock for shear-strength testing via the LabTrack incoming queue, with each entry carrying a 48-hour turnaround SLA from receipt; the lot is held-at-receipt and pick-release is blocked on both queue and dock sides until the shear result posts in LabTrack. This was set up on 2026-11-13 per [[tessa-nguyen]], verified against the incoming-inspection SOP, with no separate document created [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-restock-shear-gate].

Separately, for every incoming Vantek adhesive lot from the November 2026 restock onward, 2 tubes per lot are pulled at the dock before put-away, taken from two different cases on the pallet, each labeled with the lot number, receipt date, and "RETAINED." The LabTrack retention record must be entered the same day as receipt, with retention date set to the receipt date rather than the test date. This rule is sourced from the incoming-inspection SOP's retained-sample section, verified 2026-11-13 by [[tessa-nguyen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-retained-sample-pull-rule].

## Readiness Sweep Reporting

During the scheduled 15:30 readiness sweep on 2026-11-12 (the first afternoon run post-cutover), LabTrack's export path was found responding normally alongside stable [[nexbin]] production, [[zone-b]] live since 07:42, [[stockpro]] shutdown proceeding as scheduled, nominal carrier/EDI feeds, and no new errors; the only open item was carried-forward vendor case NB-4471. The report was delivered to [[maya-chen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-nov12-1530-clean].

## Ad-hoc Query and Documentation Preferences

When [[tessa-nguyen]] requests a quick ad-hoc LabTrack rowcount or spot-check pull rather than a standing report, the Quality Assistant should just report the resulting number and anomalies verbally or inline without creating a standing document, per her 2026-11-06 instruction that there was "no need to write this up as anything permanent, just wanted the number" [cite:memoryAtom:f-tessa-adhoc-pull-no-writeup-preference].

Relatedly, near-identical memory notes restating the same already-confirmed LabTrack setting or finding (e.g., lot filter ALL, `include_archived` false, paging quirks) should not be saved repeatedly within one session; [[tessa-nguyen]] explicitly pushed back on 2026-11-13 during the retained-sample sweep, asking why the same things kept being saved over and over and stating to "just get it right once" — each stable finding should be saved once and only re-saved if it actually changes [cite:memoryAtom:f-avoid-redundant-duplicate-memory-saves].

See also: [[tessa-nguyen]], [[maya-chen]], [[nexbin]], [[stockpro]], [[vantek-adhesives]], [[zone-b]], [[zone-c]], [[zone-d]], [[receiving]]

pages.title: Leo Kirkwood
pages.summary: Leo Kirkwood is the purchasing coordinator and owns the Purchasing Assistant agent, which handles POs and receipts .
pages.content:
Also known as: Leo, Leo Kirkwood

## Role

Leo Kirkwood is the purchasing coordinator and owns the Purchasing Assistant agent, which handles POs and receipts [cite:memoryAtom:f-leo-kirkwood-purchasing-coordinator]. He is one of the two recipients of the daily dispatch digest, alongside [[maya-chen]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-leo-kirkwood-full-name].

## Vantek Adhesives Management

Leo runs a weekly [[vantek-adhesives]] inbound review meeting with the Purchasing Assistant, held Tuesdays at 10:30, with the first review taking place November 3, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-inbound-review-schedule]. When Leo is out, [[jonas]] can release Vantek Adhesives purchase orders since he knows the account, per the purchasing page [cite:memoryAtom:f-jonas-vantek-po-backup].

As of November 11, 2026, per Leo, Vantek Adhesives' minimum order quantity is 30 cases per order, correcting a previously recorded 20-case minimum [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-vantek-minimum-order-30-correction]. Leo was notified on 2026-11-11 that Vantek receiving instructions are superseded by the new inbound receiving standard starting with the first post-cutover receipt, and that the dock should work from the [[receiving]] standard only [cite:memoryAtom:f-leo-notified-receiving-standard]. Under [[maya-chen]]'s dock standing orders saved November 13, 2026, Leo books the delivery slot for every inbound Vantek adhesive delivery once the carrier confirms, and dispatch confirms back to Leo and Maya [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-inbound-booking-rule].

## Purchasing Operations

On November 9, 2026, Leo ran a full supplier price list diff across the entire active supplier catalog (~1,200 unique SKUs, ~1,500 rows before dedup): adhesive-line SKUs showed 2-6% price increases, sealants were mostly flat to 1%, and no anomalies rose to escalation; the output was kept as a working reference diff file rather than a standing price update [cite:memoryAtom:f-purchasing-full-catalog-price-diff-nov9].

Effective November 11, 2026, per Leo, the open-PO tracker was renamed to the "inbound schedule," remaining the same underlying sheet with a new tab layout, with all purchasing-page references updated accordingly [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-open-po-tracker-renamed-inbound-schedule].

Effective November 11, 2026, per Leo, [[griploc-275]]'s reorder point was lowered from 90 cases to 75 cases because peak season demand was settling and 90 was leaving too much stock sitting; the open-PO/inbound schedule threshold and PO suggestion logic use 75 cases from this date forward [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-griploc-275-reorder-point-75-nov11].

For the receiving PO tag mapping, the target [[nexbin]] environment is production only, with nexbin-uat and nexbin-stage excluded as test-only per [[owen]]'s integration notes, confirmed with Leo on November 11, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-nexbin-po-tag-mapping-production-only].

On November 6, 2026, Leo created a second, duplicate copy of the Purchasing Assistant agent (ag-purchasing-copy) with an identical display name while testing agent setup; it answered two PO questions and was never used again [cite:memoryAtom:f-ag-purchasing-copy-origin].

The Q4 Carrier RFP Draft, authored by [[maya-chen]], was abandoned as of the Nov 7, 2026 revision because peak season and the [[nexbin]] cutover took priority; its carrier list section remains blank because Leo's Q3 spend-by-carrier pull was never received [cite:memoryAtom:f-q4-carrier-rfp-abandoned].

For staffing questions, including from Leo or [[sam]], the peak staffing scratch document is invalid and must not be used; the warehouse staffing plan document should be used instead [cite:memoryAtom:f-peak-staffing-scratch-doc-invalid].

## Dispatch Digest Reception

As one of the two recipients, Leo received the [[dispatch-digest-agent]] digest on November 12, 2026, reporting 38 pallets staged overnight, 0 holds flagged, and 3 confirmed carrier pickups with no blocking issue, so no update was made to the [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov12-dispatch-digest-episode]. He also received the November 15, 2026 digest describing a quiet Sunday morning with 10 pallets staged, two confirmed pickups, and no exceptions [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov15-dispatch-digest-episode]. On November 10, 2026, a scheduling anomaly caused two separate dispatch digest runs for the same date, resulting in two distinct digests sent to Maya and Leo the same day [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov10-duplicate-digest-run-anomaly].

## Disputed

On November 11, 2026, Leo instructed that Vantek Adhesives' planning lead time stay at 10 business days, reasoning that two fast deliveries during peak season don't establish a trend justifying a lower lead time [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-vantek-lead-time-kept-10-despite-fast-deliveries]. This stands in tension with the fact that the last two Vantek receipts actually landed in 6 business days, which would suggest a shorter lead time [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-vantek-lead-time-kept-10-despite-fast-deliveries]. This conflict is unresolved.

See also: [[vantek-adhesives]], [[maya-chen]], [[griploc-275]], [[dispatch-digest-agent]], [[jonas]]

## Additional facts
- As of Nov 4, 2026, Brightwell opened an evaluation of Halvorsen Packaging as a possible secondary supplier for corrugated void-fill and carton stock (corrugated sheets, void-fill paper, stretch wrap). [cite:memoryAtom:f-halvorsen-packaging-evaluation-opened]

pages.summary: Maya Chen is the ops lead and workspace owner for Brightwell Supply Co, overseeing dock scheduling, purchasing notifications, the CL Rollout cutover, readiness reporting, and the support queue digest program .
pages.content:
## Role

Maya Chen is the ops lead and workspace owner for Brightwell Supply Co, overseeing dock scheduling, purchasing notifications, the [[cl-rollout]] cutover, readiness reporting, and the support queue digest program [cite:memoryAtom:f-maya-chen-ops-lead-owner].

## Standing Rules and Preferences

She requires SOP-type documents to carry the version date in the title (e.g. "CL Rollout cutover runbook (2026-11-02)") for identifiability [cite:memoryAtom:f-sop-title-versioning-rule].

She holds a general preference to be copied on notifications whenever any PO's delivery/due date changes, not limited to [[vantek-adhesives]] orders, since she plans dock/door scheduling off these dates [cite:memoryAtom:f-maya-chen-po-date-notify-preference-general].

Per dock standing orders (saved 2026-11-13), every inbound Vantek adhesive delivery must be booked with dispatch by 15:00 the day before, with a forklift and second [[receiving]] staffer assigned; [[leo]] books the slot once the carrier confirms, dispatch confirms back to Leo and Maya, and unbooked deliveries wait in the yard [cite:memoryAtom:f-vantek-inbound-booking-rule].

Effective 2026-11-11, she redirected Pick-confirm SOP sign-off to [[tessa-nguyen]], who now owns quality and support; future revisions go to Tessa [cite:memoryAtom:f-pick-confirm-sop-signoff-tessa-13].

## Purchase Order Notifications

She was notified with [[jonas]] when [[vantek-adhesives]] pushed PO-2026-4466's due date ([[griploc-275]], 30 cases) from Nov 6 to Nov 10, 2026, with the ERP updated [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4466-date-push].

Per her standing preference, she was notified when PO-2026-4489 (hex bolts M10, 40 cases, no partials) moved up from Nov 13 to Nov 11, 2026 after early vendor delivery; Jonas was notified separately for a pending backorder release [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4489-early-delivery-date-change].

She and Jonas were both notified when PO-2026-4512 (SL-410 sealant cartridges, 12 cases, no partials) was pushed by the vendor from Nov 16 to Nov 19, 2026, with the due date field updated [cite:memoryAtom:f-po-2026-4512-date-push].

## Abandoned Documents

The "Q4 Carrier RFP Draft," authored by Maya Chen, was abandoned as of the Nov 7, 2026 revision since peak season and the [[nexbin]] cutover took priority; it remains as-is, with its carrier list blank because [[leo]]'s Q3 spend-by-carrier pull was never received [cite:memoryAtom:f-q4-carrier-rfp-abandoned].

As of Nov 8, 2026, she also abandoned the "Zone B migration draft," leaving most sections as "[insert]" placeholders, and moved to working directly in the [[cl-rollout]] runbook; this draft is not a current source of [[zone-b]]/CL Rollout status [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-b-migration-draft-abandoned].

## Readiness Sweeps and CL Rollout Reporting

Maya Chen is the standing recipient of twice-daily [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]] sweep reports. The procedure requires opening the current cycle document, dispatching Purchasing for the round covering inbound receipts through cutover, collecting Purchasing's section and pending role updates, reconciling standing-value changes, publishing an updated cycle version, and reporting status to her [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-procedure-steps].

Clean sweeps reported to her: Nov 9 15:30 ([[nexbin]] uat/stage healthy, no new [[stockpro]] cases, [[duraline]] consolidation-plan retraction non-blocking) [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov9-1530-sweep-clean-pass]; Nov 12 15:30 (NexBin production stable, [[zone-b]] live since 07:42, StockPro shutdown on schedule, [[labtrack-lims]] export normal, only carried-forward case NB-4471 open) [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-nov12-1530-clean]; Nov 14 15:30 (Zone B pick-confirm green, StockPro legacy queue zero stuck records, LIMS export on schedule, normal queue depth) [cite:memoryAtom:f-sweep-nov14-1530-clean]; and the Nov 15 15:30 final PM sweep for cutover cycle day 14 (no open NexBin incidents, zero carrier/pick exceptions, normal service desk depth, no open action items), after which no new cycle round was opened [cite:memoryAtom:f-final-readiness-sweep-pm-nov15].

## Disputed

On Nov 12, 2026, [[zone-c]]'s location diff initially showed 3 mismatches in aisle 14 from stale bin renumbering, fixed source-side by [[owen]]; the re-run diff came back clean at 1,140/1,140. Despite this, Maya Chen chose to hold the Zone C live flip until Nov 13, 2026 — unresolved against the clean diff outcome [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-c-diff-clean-flip-held].

## Dispatch Digests

Maya Chen, with [[leo]], is a standing recipient of the [[dispatch-digest-agent]]'s scheduled digest. Reported runs: Nov 12, 2026 (38 pallets staged, 0 holds, 3 confirmed carrier pickups) [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov12-dispatch-digest-episode]; and Nov 15, 2026 Sunday (10 pallets staged, two confirmed pickups, no exceptions) [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov15-dispatch-digest-episode].

On Nov 10, 2026, a scheduling anomaly produced two separate digest runs for the same date under the same 06:00 label — one pallet-focused, one outbound-count with an added manifest reconciliation step — both sent to Maya and Leo [cite:memoryAtom:f-nov10-duplicate-digest-run-anomaly].

## Support Queue Digest

Maya Chen is a standing recipient (with [[tessa-nguyen]] and [[jonas]]) of the [[support-queue-digest]], produced first by the Support Assistant and later by the [[service-desk-assistant]]. Despite a Nov 6, 2026 request to flag the new SHORT refund reason code for Maya and Jonas, the Nov 7, 2026 08:00 digest's Callouts read "none" and omitted SHORT entirely [cite:memoryAtom:f-short-code-flag-omitted-2026-11-07].

Subsequent runs delivered to Maya: Nov 10, 2026 (97 open tickets, mixed reason codes, nothing over $200) [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-10]; Nov 11, 2026 (14 open tickets, zero pending refunds, no escalations) [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-11]; the Nov 13, 2026 format revision to v2 (fixed Callouts heading, 150-word budget, Maya/Tessa/Jonas recipients) [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-format-v2]; the Service Desk Assistant's first digest under that format, same day (94 open tickets, 6 refund requests with 3 over $200 routed to [[priya-rao]] under the hypercare rule, 1 SHORT ticket) [cite:memoryAtom:f-first-digest-run-2026-11-13]; Nov 14, 2026 Saturday (11 open tickets, zero refunds pending, one resolved +SHORT ticket) [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-14]; and Nov 15, 2026 Sunday (61 open tickets, 3 refund requests pending, one $240 refund routed to Priya Rao, and a Callouts note on [[duraline-industrial-supply]]'s interim contact Kwame Asante through November 30) [cite:memoryAtom:f-digest-run-2026-11-15].

See also: [[cl-rollout]], [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]], [[jonas]], [[leo]], [[tessa-nguyen]], [[vantek-adhesives]], [[nexbin]], [[zone-c]], [[dispatch-digest-agent]], [[support-queue-digest]]

pages.content:
## Overview
NexBin is the bin/inventory management system being cut over to at the [[stockton-warehouse]] as part of [[cl-rollout]], replacing [[stockpro]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-runbook-scope]. The CL Rollout cutover runbook covers only the sequence, timeline, freeze window, rollback criterion, roles, and contacts for the NexBin cutover, and explicitly excludes supplier, finance, or account matters [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-runbook-scope].

## Cutover Timeline
The go-live at Stockton warehouse moved to Thursday Nov 12, 2026 at 05:00, per the Nov 10, 2026 runbook revision, after a final data-migration dry run in nexbin-stage surfaced a bin-mapping error requiring an extra day to fix and re-verify [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-golive-nov12-correction]. On Nov 2, 2026, pre-cutover checks found the [[stockpro]] throughput baseline steady with no anomalies and no blocking tickets open in the NexBin UAT queue [cite:memoryAtom:f-cl-rollout-baseline-check-episode]. [[zone-b]]'s actual production activation occurred at 07:42 on Nov 12, 2026, later than the planned 05:00 time, but was confirmed stable per that day's 15:30 readiness sweep [cite:memoryAtom:f-zone-b-actual-activation-0742].

Per NexBin Cutover Checklist v3.3 (mirrored Nov 12, 2026), rollback trigger steps were renumbered after inserting a new pre-cutover step 11 (freeze inbound receipts at 12:00 the day before cutover, owned by Brightwell/Customer, to lock counted stock levels and reduce reconciliation variance) [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-v33-freeze-inbound-receipts-step]. Rollback must now be initiated if go-live validation fails at step 18 (previously step 17), or if post-cutover reconciliation variance at step 23 exceeds 2% of counted SKU lines; the 2% threshold and 4-hour reconciliation timing requirement are otherwise unchanged from v3.2 [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-checklist-v33-rollback-step-renumbering].

As of Nov 6, 2026, Brightwell still needed vendor confirmation from NexBin on cutover checklist steps 12-13 — scheduling vendor case queue coverage for cutover day and confirming the rollback environment snapshot was taken — both NexBin-owned steps Brightwell could not self-certify [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-vendor-confirmation-pending-steps-12-13].

## Data Retention
NexBin retains bin history for 400 days as a platform default (not a tenant-specific override), compared with [[stockpro]], which purges bin history at 90 days; this was confirmed by [[owen]] via a direct StockPro bin-history query on Nov 3, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-stockpro-vs-nexbin-retention].

## Exports and Environments
The bin column in the NexBin inbound receipts export is named `location_ref`, originally documented on 2026-11-04 and re-verified on 2026-11-13 via a live sample export, confirming the field name has not been renamed since [[zone-b]] went live [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-export-bin-column-location-ref]. When a full bin export is requested (e.g. for a location-mapping crosswalk), the expected deliverable is raw JSON per-zone files covering every bin record across all zones with no filtering or summarization [cite:memoryAtom:f-bin-export-raw-json-preference].

A full post-cutover stock position export was pulled from NexBin on 2026-11-13 across Zones A-D plus overflow bins, totaling 1,743 rows (640 rows Zone A/B combined, 410 rows [[zone-c]], 505 rows [[zone-d]], 188 rows overflow), merged into the document "Post-Cutover Stock Position Export - Nov 13" [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-post-cutover-export-nov13]. Requesting the full all-zone export as a single combined call times out due to payload size; it must be pulled as paged per-zone batches and then merged into one file [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-combined-request-timeout]. Even though the underlying pull is split into per-zone batches, the delivered result should be a single clean merged file rather than multiple separate batch files [cite:memoryAtom:f-stock-export-single-merged-file-preference]. During the Nov 6, 2026 all-zone inbound reconciliation pull, the export repeatedly timed out with 502 errors on [[zone-d]] pages under heavy parallel-testing load, requiring 2-3 retries per page [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-export-zone-timeout-under-load]. During the Nov 13, 2026 stock position export, the [[zone-c]] page repeatedly returned 502 gateway timeout errors under load, which cleared after reducing the request page size [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-zonec-502-timeout-nov13].

For receiving PO tag mapping, the target NexBin environment is production only; nexbin-uat and nexbin-stage are excluded as test-only, per [[owen]]'s integration notes and confirmed with [[leo]] on November 11, 2026 [cite:memoryAtom:f-f-nexbin-po-tag-mapping-production-only]. This applies to the [[receiving]] workflow.

## Known Issues and Fixes
When NexBin's `/exports/lots` endpoint returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests, the standing fix is a retry-with-backoff wrapper around the client call; an earlier throttle-only rate-limit adjustment was found insufficient under load and was superseded by the backoff-wrapper fix, per [[owen]]'s integration notes [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-429-backoff-fix]. NexBin case NB-0011 (bulk bin import batch-size limit) is resolved: batch size 200 avoids the API limit entirely and is the standing standard for the bulk bin import job, with exponential backoff (base 2s) retained only as a fallback [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-nb0011-bulk-import-resolved]. Vendor case NB-4471 with NexBin remained open as of the 15:30 readiness sweep on 2026-11-12, with no vendor update since that morning's check-in, and was carried forward as the one open item on the [[cl-rollout-readiness-cycle-document]] [cite:memoryAtom:f-nb-4471-open-vendor-case].

An EDI 856 replay of 812 pending ASN records from [[stockpro]] against nexbin-uat on 2026-11-09 resulted in 761 accepted, 4 malformed-segment rejects, and 50 batch-3 records unresolved after 40 consecutive failed retries (timeouts and 502 errors); the same payload succeeded immediately against nexbin-stage, confirming the payload was well-formed and the failure was localized to nexbin-uat under load. This result does not confirm nexbin-uat capacity is adequate and says nothing about production environment behavior; the user directed the agent to stop retrying and leave batch 3 for review after lunch [cite:memoryAtom:f-edi-856-replay-nov9-nexbin-uat].

## Reconciliation and Data Quality
A full inbound receipts reconciliation run on November 6, 2026 between the NexBin export and [[stockpro]] receipts log across all zones covered 2,522 NexBin lines versus 1,976 StockPro lines, finding 356 mismatches (about 14%): 210 quantity variances under 5 units, 98 timing offsets where NexBin logged a receipt a day later than StockPro, and 48 lines present only in NexBin from parallel cutover test activity that never flowed through the legacy path; 22 mismatches were adhesive-category lines with no unusual pattern. No corrective action was taken and the full mismatch list was exported for review [cite:memoryAtom:f-nexbin-stockpro-reconciliation-nov2026].

A spot-check on 2026-11-13 compared 20 of 92 [[griploc-275]] rows from the NexBin export against [[stockpro]] bin records: 17 matched exactly, and 3 showed small variances of a few units attributed to picks logged between the export windows rather than a real discrepancy [cite:memoryAtom:f-griploc275-spotcheck-nov13].

The [[labtrack-lims]] export column `location_ref` (appearing the week of Nov 9, 2026) maps to the LabTrack-internal storage bin, not the NexBin bin location, and should not be assumed to align with NexBin location codes until a mapping is confirmed; a blank value means the lot has not had a putaway scan recorded in LabTrack yet, not necessarily a data gap [cite:memoryAtom:f-labtrack-location-ref-mapping].

In the Pick-confirm SOP, lot number capture from the container label (step 2) applies only to adhesives and sealants categories; other categories skip that check, and [[stockpro]] bins not yet migrated to NexBin continue on the legacy pick sheet process
